local_derivations.name: Finite Fourier separation and closure
local_derivations.argument: Fix the stage U and a finite coefficient field containing the finite constituent data. In the finite-dimensional characteristic-zero modular-form space, all Fourier coefficient functionals jointly separate points. Their kernels therefore have a finite subfamily with zero intersection (successively lower dimension until zero). If every member of the Hecke/diamond-generated O-module has integral coefficients, this finite coordinate map embeds the module into O^r. A submodule of O^r is finitely generated since O is a DVR. In its finite-dimensional ambient space it is closed: a finite generating map O^s to that space has compact image. No saturation, integral constituent projector, or identification with every reduced expansion follows or is needed.
local_derivations.premises: Actual modularity of all blocks, finite-dimensionality and q-expansion uniqueness, complete finite coefficient field, and integrality of all good Hecke/diamond translates established in the caller.

local_derivations.name: Finite-quotient approximation
local_derivations.argument: For a fixed Galois element and fixed finite set of constituent representations, use stable lattices and finite mod-uniformizer^a quotients. Chebotarev supplies a good Frobenius conjugacy class matching the simultaneous quotient, outside the fixed bad set. As a increases, its scalar traces and determinants converge to those of the chosen element. At good primes these are the actual Hecke and cyclotomic-times-diamond operators. The preceding closed module is therefore preserved by their limits. Equal good eigensystems have equal continuous scalar trace/determinant functions by the same approximation, so old multiplicity spaces do not require individual projectors. The scalar attached to one two-dimensional constituent acts identically on each of its old multiplicity copies; it is not the trace or determinant of the direct sum of all copies. Congruent residual constituents are not separated by idempotents.
local_derivations.premises: Both cuspidal and Eisenstein representations and their good trace/determinant comparisons must first be supplied; no infinite-level Chebotarev theorem or uniform prime bound is asserted.

local_derivations.name: Actual Eisenstein two-character realization
local_derivations.argument: For a basis series E_(2,alpha,beta), equation5.3.1 gives a_n=sum_(d|n) beta(d)alpha(n/d)d. At p not dividing the final level, the divisor sum satisfies a_(pn)+p*alpha(p)beta(p)*a_(n/p)=(alpha(p)+p*beta(p))*a_n. This follows on p-powers by the two-root geometric-sum recurrence and then multiplicativity for n prime to p. The constant coefficient is zero when alpha is nontrivial; when alpha=1 its good Hecke equation has the same multiplier1+p*beta(p). Substitution q->q^t commutes with good T_p when p does not divide t, preserving all old multiplicities. For the exceptional weight2 trivial-character basis E2(q)-tE2(q^t), the same formal divisor-sum computation gives good eigenvalue1+p, including composite t. Associate to alpha,beta the finite Galois characters via their cyclotomic residue action. The direct sum alpha plus beta*chi_cyc then has arithmetic-Frobenius trace alpha(p)+p*beta(p) and determinant p*alpha(p)beta(p). These are the actual good Hecke and cyclotomic-diamond values. No irreducibility or cuspidality is claimed for this representation.
local_derivations.premises: Stein5.8–5.9 basis theorem, stated parity/level conditions, actual good prime p outside N and2, and cyclotomic character with arithmetic Frobenius p. The p|level operators and arbitrary composite-t all-Hecke eigenform assertions are not used.

elementary_inputs.name: Principal local quadratic ideals
elementary_inputs.argument: After identifying the faithful two-dimensional representation of a quadratic field F/Qp with its regular one-dimensional F-module, an OF-stable full Zp lattice I is a fractional ideal. Its nonzero valuations have a minimum a because I is a lattice. Choose x in I of valuation a. Then xOF is contained in I by stability, and every y in I has y/x in OF by minimality. Thus I=xOF. This uses the valuation-ring description of the ring of integers of a finite local field, retained as foundational local-field data. For the split algebra Qp x Qp, its two labelled integral idempotents split I into two rank-one Zp lattices; each is principal by the same Zp valuation argument.

elementary_inputs.name: Actual split cyclic lattice pair
elementary_inputs.argument: Use the actual integral labelled projectors of the split model. They split both lattices in the cyclic index-p^e pair into their two eigendirections. Write the two nonnegative elementary exponents a,b. Cyclicity gives min(a,b)=0 and the index gives a+b=e. Hence exactly (e,0) and (0,e). These are labelled embeddings modulo order units; passing to the full normalizer would identify possibilities and is not allowed.

remaining_foundations: Valuation ring and discrete valuation on a finite extension of Qp
The actual enhanced cyclic level-p^e structure and its identification with the split Eichler lattice pair
The published division cyclic model and the specified field-embedding conjugacy theorem
boundaries: No use of an outgoing embedding-count conclusion as an input
No claim of conjugacy modulo the full normalizer
No fresh proof of the global CM reduction or theta comparison

claims.assertion: One maximal-order local embedding orbit away from N ell0.
claims.argument: For a quadratic field L/Q_p, an O_L-stable Z_p lattice inside L is a fractional O_L ideal: multiplying by a common denominator puts it in O_L, and stability makes it an ideal. O_L is a DVR, so it is principal. For L=Q_p×Q_p, integral idempotents split the lattice as two rank-one Z_p lattices, also a principal fractional ideal of Z_p×Z_p. Changing the fractional ideal generator identifies the lattices; with the usual regular representation of L, this gives one GL_2(Z_p)-conjugacy class of integral embeddings into the maximal matrix order.
inputs: Integers of a finite extension of Q_p form a DVR; Z_p lattices admit a common denominator.
Every faithful two-dimensional representation of the quadratic etale algebra is its rank-one regular module.
Conjugating the lattice model identifies embeddings into End_Zp(lattice).

claims.assertion: Exactly two oriented split Eichler lattice-pair types.
claims.argument: The integral split idempotents decompose each of the two stable lattices. Scale the larger lattice to Z_p⊕Z_p. The smaller is p^a Z_p⊕p^b Z_p with a,b nonnegative. Its index is p^(a+b)=p^e, while cyclicity of the quotient forces min(a,b)=0. As e>=1, the only types are (e,0) and (0,e). A conjugacy respecting the labelled quadratic embedding acts through its centralizer and cannot swap the two labelled idempotents. The same argument works at two because the actual integral projectors are assumed.
inputs: The actual local quadratic algebra is split at p|N.
The actual Eichler order is End(L) intersect End(Lprime) for a cyclic index-p^e lattice pair.
The spectral idempotents are integral at two, as constructed in the caller.

claims.assertion: Two residue orientations in the division case.
claims.argument: The retained generic division theorem gives D=(L/Q_p,pi), L unramified quadratic, with O_D=O_L⊕O_L Pi, Pi^2=pi and Pi a=Frob(a) Pi. Its residue field is F_(p^2). Inner conjugation by an O_D unit acts trivially on that commutative residue field, while Pi induces its nontrivial Frobenius. By Skolem–Noether any two embeddings of L in D are D^times-conjugate. Every nonzero conjugating element is Pi^n times a unit; parity of n is its residue orientation, and even powers are central powers of pi. Thus exactly the two residue embeddings classify the O_D-unit orbits.
inputs: Generic unramified-quadratic division model and unique maximal order, supplied by ACTIVE-CJ-LOCAL-PRIMITIVE-LOCAL-DIVISION.
Skolem–Noether for the quadratic field in the central simple quaternion algebra.
Actual local field F_p is unramified quadratic at ell0.
